# DELF B1 Preparation Note
## Oral opinion practice
This classroom activity is designed for DELF B1 preparation; it is not an official examination prompt or scoring grid. Give a brief oral presentation expressing your opinion on a familiar community topic. State your position and support it with two reasons or examples. Then respond to follow-up questions from the examiner.
## Feedback points
Feedback should consider whether the position is clear, whether the reasons or examples support it, whether the presentation is organized and understandable, and whether the speaker responds relevantly to follow-up questions. These points are for this activity and do not reproduce an official scoring grid.

# DALF C1 Preparation Note
## Source-based writing exercise
This course exercise is designed for DALF C1 preparation; it is not an official examination prompt or scoring grid. Read two short texts on a public issue. First write a synthesis that presents their main points neutrally. Then write an argumentative response that states and defends your own position. Keep the synthesis distinct from personal opinion.
## Feedback criteria
Feedback should consider fidelity to the two texts, neutrality in the synthesis, a clear distinction between synthesis and personal response, logical organization, support for the position, and precise language. These criteria are for this course exercise and do not reproduce an official scoring grid.
